main_body: Long wooden water trough: brown rim, blue water surface, then a plank front face
top_band: Rows 4-10 read as the top: a brown back rim (row 4), light-to-mid blue water (rows 5-8), and a brown front rim lip (rows 9-10). The scan lumps rows 8-10 together because dark blue and the brown lip share a similar L.
evidence: Column scan: back rim at row 4, water rows 5-8 with a lighter highlight at row 5 and darker blue at row 8, then a brown front rim at rows 9-10. Row 11 is a dark shadow line under the rim, which acts as the eave shadow. Rows 12-13 are the brown plank front and row 14 is the dark base. The water surface is a real visible opening of about 4 rows, and the front face is about 4 rows, so this is a top plus a front, not a flat elevation. The plank front only has a couple of painted seams and no inset detail, but the main body satisfies the contract.

style.evidence: The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels) and there are no 5x5 flat fills (0%), which counts in its favour. The piece is much thinner than the references on material ramps. The whole piece uses only 11 colours against 38-40 for the references. The water is made of flat horizontal stripes with a few sparkle pixels. The wood is just two or three tones: a plain 2-row front rim and a front face with two plank seams, with no grain or knot speckle. The median of 11 colours per tile is at the Beodeul norm, but the references reach 17-20, and this reads flatter and more banded than the stall and well. It would look thinner next to them.
